questions.prompt: What charge does an electron carry?
questions.explanation: An electron carries a -1 negative charge — the opposite of the positive proton.
questions.misconception: The positive charge belongs to protons, and electrons are never neutral or variable — every electron is always -1.

questions.prompt: Where do electrons live in an atom?
options: They float at fixed spots outside the atom
questions.explanation: Electrons orbit the nucleus in organized layers called shells, far outside the dense core.
questions.misconception: The nucleus is packed with protons and neutrons — electrons stay in the shells, orbiting far outside the core.

questions.prompt: Which electrons are involved in chemical reactions?
options: The outermost electrons — the valence electrons
questions.explanation: The outermost electrons — the valence electrons — are the ones shared, lost, or gained during reactions.
questions.misconception: It is never the inner electrons (or the nuclear particles) that react — the chemistry happens with the outermost-shell electrons.

questions.prompt: How does the mass of an electron compare to a proton?
options: It has no mass at all
questions.explanation: An electron is tiny — about 1,836 times lighter than a proton — which is why nearly all of an atom's mass is in the nucleus.
questions.misconception: Electrons do have mass, but almost none compared to protons and neutrons — the nucleus carries nearly all the atom's weight.
